speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for National Development what are the eligibility conditions for divorcees with shared care and control of their children to purchase a subsidised HDB flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Those awarded shared care and control of their children share the right to list the children in their flat application.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is rare, as care and control is usually awarded to one parent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This ensures fairness to both parties, as HDB is not in a position to determine which parent should exercise the right to list the child.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Nonetheless, those who cannot reach an agreement with their ex-spouse may approach HDB to discuss their options.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that the shared care and control is actually a Court ruling so that the children following a divorce will be able to live with both parties.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But then, our housing policies now penalise them for having this shared care and control, instead of sole care and control.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am wondering if MND can work with the Courts so that we can align our policies so that the judgment that is obtained can actually be enforced and be feasible.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The second clarification is, HDB had initially said that they have removed the time bar as they realised that it caused friction between both parties because they cannot decide on who will get the subsidised housing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They also said they had removed the time bar in the best interest of the children involved in the divorce.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But now that we are back to the ex-spousal consent on who can list the children as occupiers, are we not back to square one again?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And would the Senior Parliamentary Secretary agree that this would again lead to friction between both parties, because they now have to again decide on who will get the subsidised housing?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Time bar aside, divorced couples with shared care and control of their child, as I have mentioned, are still required to obtain their ex-spouse's written agreement before they apply for a flat.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is because both parents have equal rights to buy a flat with their child and HDB is not in a position to determine which parent should exercise the right.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, we recognise that each of the family's circumstances are different and it is best to take an approach where flexibility can be exercised to meet the specific circumstances and needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Speaker, I thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for her clarification.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I would just like to take this opportunity to echo Mr Louis Ng's concerns on this matter.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am a practising divorce lawyer and this is a matter I see fairly commonly.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Even if the order is not a shared order, even if it is share and control to one parent, there is always this disagreement and issues with regard to the housing arrangements because only one party can list and use the children's name.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I would just want to highlight and stress the difficulties that parties have.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This becomes an issue of contention because they have difficulties arranging for their housing later, especially in shared care and control arrangements.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Parties have difficulties resolving it in a divorce.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, it does not help in the resolution of the divorce, if we do not figure out how we can lay out plans that can help parties moving forward.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There is already this housing guidance arrangement that is given to parties at divorce.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: They have to fill it up and sign it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: From my experience and from anecdotal evidence given by clients who have gone through the process, depending on the officer, the advice given may not necessarily be as thorough and helpful.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, I believe that in circumstances where there is a divorce, it would be helpful if parties are given a very clear outcome, a very clear option that is available to them, especially at that stage before they actually go through the whole divorce process so that they can see how much loan they can take out, how much monies they have, what are their options.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: They have all these in broad terms but it does not really help because they just give rough figures or, sometimes, to the extent that they would not even have an indication of the housing loan eligibility because they do not have the divorce order yet.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I think there is hesitance in fixing a certain amount before they actually know the full picture.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: To be fair to the parties, you really need to guide them along.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, one, I would suggest that you review the process in respect of housing guidance to help divorced parties; and, two, I would just echo Mr Louis Ng's point that we may need to review this position about making it an exception because the policy itself does not gel with the principle of a shared care and control arrangement.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Because the parties are actually ordered to be able to allow the children to live with them.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, the idea is that, half the time, they are living with the father and half the time they are living with the mother.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: If they do not have proper housing —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can the Member keep the question more concise, please?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: If they do not have proper housing, they will face some difficulties.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We understand the concern that mutual agreement might be difficult and, as I have mentioned, we will exercise flexibility for those who face financial hardship or lack family support.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will take a needs-based approach and take each family's circumstance into account.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will ensure that parents with shared care and control have options to provide housing for themselves and their children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, any parties undergoing a divorce may seek advice from HDB on their housing options.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Does the Ministry work together with the Family Courts in terms of coming to a mutual set of guidelines?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Because, in recent months, there have been more cases of shared care and control that I have seen and we also have cases that we have come across with limited tenure shared care and control.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For example, a resident of mine was given shared care and control of the children with her spouse for only 10 months and she was told by the Courts that she needs to resolve her housing situation within these 10 months.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This was quite distinct from all the other judgments, in terms of divorce cases that I have seen in the last decade or so.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can I suggest that, at least, we waive this ex-spousal consent for children to be listed as occupiers, if the other party has moved on?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Following the divorce, they now own a private property or they own a subsidised housing, which means that they have re-married.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the ex-spousal consent then be waived for the other party?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I know of cases where both refused to sign and both ended up renting homes, because that is the whole reason why they divorced in the first place, they could not agree on things.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, can we at least waive ex-spousal consent for these cases?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I have said, we will look at each case on a case-by-case basis.
